items.name: Anushka Jena
items.heading: The police station
items.body:
“Ma’am, you’ll have to come to court every day. Are you sure?”

For many, that question can make pursuing a dispute feel more daunting than walking away. What begins as a fight for what is right can become years of expenses, uncertainty and lost peace. But resolving a dispute shouldn't always mean preparing for a legal battle. Mediation offers another way: a conversation where people can work towards a resolution and retain a say in the outcome. Somewhere in India, someone is about to drop their case. Not because they were wrong. Because fighting costs money, and years of peace. UnLitigate your disputes. Choose your agency.

image.alt: Quiet conversation at a desk, stand-in for Anushka's founding story

items.name: Madhur
items.heading: The wait
items.body: A dispute should not swallow a whole year of someone's life. Watching people wait — and then give up — is what made this feel urgent. Pune is where that observation became operations: supervised student mediation in a city that moves fast and still gets stuck.

image.alt: Campus walkway, stand-in for Madhur's story

items.name: Prakhar
items.heading: After it began
items.body: People deserve a first step that does not feel like a fight. Partnerships are how a student initiative becomes something a worried family can trust — precise about what is live, what is a pilot, and what is still being built.

image.alt: City street at warm light, stand-in for Prakhar's story
